title: GTA6 Hub: 20 Years Later, Rockstar’s Bully Deserves a Sequel
description: Polygon reflects on Rockstar's innovative classic Bully 20 years later, discussing its unique legacy and the ongoing desire for a true sequel.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Looking Back at a Rockstar Classic

Within the illustrious development history of Rockstar Games, few titles hold as unique and enduring a place in fan hearts as *Bully* (also known as *Canis Canem Edit*). According to a recent report by Polygon, twenty years after its initial release, *Bully* remains one of Rockstar's most innovative and unique games ever created—sparking renewed conversation about whether the cult-classic masterpiece is long overdue for a proper sequel.

## The Unique Appeal of Bullworth Academy

What made *Bully* stand out in the gaming landscape was not massive explosive action, but its micro-scaled, highly detailed focus on boarding school life. Playing as protagonist Jimmy Hopkins, players navigated the social hierarchies, cliques, classes, and mischief of Bullworth Academy. This creative approach to a localized open-world structure proved that Rockstar could deliver engaging narratives outside of traditional crime syndicates.

While Rockstar's main focus is heavily anchored on the upcoming launch of *GTA6*, the enduring legacy of games like *Bully* highlights a broader industry sentiment: fans deeply miss the studio's willingness to tackle smaller-scale, distinct thematic experiments alongside their blockbuster giants.

## A Legacy Waiting for Its Continuation

As anticipation reaches an all-time high for *GTA6*, looking back at past gems like *Bully* serves as a reminder of Rockstar's unmatched creative range. Polygon's retrospective emphasizes that two decades on, this brilliant sandbox title still lacks the sequel it truly deserved, leaving an unfilled gap in Rockstar's historic catalog.

## Editor's Take

*Bully* proved Rockstar was about more than just crime simulators. While all eyes are on *GTA6* right now, a modern return to Bullworth Academy would be a dream come true for longtime fans of the studio's narrative versatility.
